title: Sales enablement playbook: positioning, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook equips Redwood Inference sellers and solutions engineers with concise positioning, competitor talking points, a recommended pitch-deck outline, indicative pricing guidance, short case studies, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ. Use this as the canonical single-sheet for enterprise and PLG motions; link to technical pages for deep-dives.

Audience: AEs, SDRs, SEs, customer success, partner reps, and marketing enablement authors.

Owner / maintenance: Go-to-market (Asha Patel). Quarterly review cadence; product and security review before major messaging changes.

Key positioning (elevator + 3 proof points)

- Elevator (30s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLMs predictable, economical, and reliable in production — whether you use our hosted API, buy reserved Dedicated capacity, or run a Private deployment in your VPC.
- Proof points:
  - Production economics: Clear levers (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles) that reduce per-token cost up to 3x compared to naive endpoints on the same GPUs.
  - Unified runtime across deployment modes: Same API, rollouts, and observability whether hosted or private — reduces dev and ops overhead for multi-environment apps.
  - Reliability and graceful degradation: Automated routing and fallback policies (model variants & regions) keep apps online under capacity pressure.

Positioning pillars (short messaging framework)

1) Developer velocity: Simple REST/SDK, streaming, function-calling, and model catalog — integrate in hours, iterate rapidly.
2) Production-grade inference: Predictable latency, throughput controls, SLOs, and per-route observability for debugging and cost attribution.
3) Cost control & optimization: Per-route batching and cache recommendations plus model/quantization guidance tied to workload profiles.
4) Deployment flexibility & compliance: Hosted for speed; Dedicated for predictability; Private for regulated workloads with KMS/HSM integration.

Competitive brief summary (one-paragraph then quick comparison table)

- Summary: Competitive landscape includes general cloud AI endpoint offerings, LLM API layers, and self-hosted inference runtimes. Redwood differentiates by combining a high-throughput, GPU-optimized runtime with developer-first APIs and enterprise controls (rollouts, SLAs, private deployments) — focused on production economics and reliability.

Quick comparator table (rows: capability; columns: Redwood / Cloud-managed endpoints / LLM API providers / Inference runtimes)

- Capabilities considered: performance & kernel optimization; unified API across hosted/dedicated/private; enterprise SLAs & private deployments; cost-optimization tooling; observability per-route; onboarding velocity

- Performance & kernel optimization: Redwood — Yes (GPU kernel selection + continuous batching); Cloud-managed — Variable; LLM API — Depends; Runtimes — Yes but ops-heavy
- Unified API across modes: Redwood — Yes; Cloud-managed — No; LLM API — Limited; Runtimes — No (customer build)
- Enterprise SLAs & Private deploy: Redwood — Hosted + Dedicated + Private (VPC/on‑prem); Cloud-managed — Hosted w/ VPC peering options; LLM API — Usually hosted; Runtimes — Self-host only
- Cost-optimization tooling: Redwood — Built-in suggestions & quantization profiles; Cloud-managed — Limited; LLM API — Rare; Runtimes — Tooling varies
- Observability per-route: Redwood — Yes (token-level, model breakdowns); Cloud-managed — Basic; LLM API — Basic; Runtimes — Custom
- Onboarding velocity: Redwood — High (quickstarts + SDKs); Cloud-managed — High; LLM API — High; Runtimes — Low (integration effort)

How to use this brief: Tailor competitor callouts to the prospect’s top pain (latency, cost, single-tenant requirements, or audit/compliance). For technical buyers emphasize kernel and batching advantages; for procurement emphasize pricing transparency and committed capacity options.

Pitch deck outline (recommended sequence and one-liners)

1) Title / Ask (1 slide): Customer name + core value proposition + CTA (trial, pilot, dedicated eval)
2) Problem (1): Rising LLM infra costs, unpredictable latency, and complex ops for multi-environment deployments
3) Market (1): LLM adoption trends + developers/ML teams needing production inference
4) Solution: Redwood Inference — hosted, dedicated, private; unified runtime and tooling
5) How it works (2): Serving runtime & kernel selection; smart routing & caching; deployment abstraction
6) Differentiators (1): Production-first developer experience, cost-aware controls, graceful degradation
7) Case study highlights (2): Short outcomes + metrics (latency, cost savings, time-to-first-API)
8) Security & compliance (1): SOC2 Type II, KMS integration, private deployment options
9) Pricing options (1): Self-serve hosted; reserved Dedicated; Private licensing + support
10) Next steps & pilot plan (1): Technical eval steps and signatures

Slide tips for SEs: keep technical appendix slides (latency profiles, kernel tuning, model variants) for deeper conversations. Use visuals: throughput graphs, before/after cost charts, and a one-line architecture diagram.

Indicative pricing guidance (use when asked for order-of-magnitude; always hand off to pricing team for firm quotes)

- Hosted (self-serve) — usage-based: example ranges (indicative):
  - Generation models: $0.002 to $0.012 per 1K tokens depending on model size and latency tier.
  - High-accuracy large models: $0.010 to $0.030 per 1K tokens (specialized workloads).
  - Embeddings: $0.0005 to $0.002 per 1K vectors (varies by model).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) — committed monthly/annual:
  - Starting point (indicative): $12,000 to $25,000 per GPU-equivalent month for reserved clusters with throughput SLAs.
  - Autoscaling and burst capacity available as add-ons; pricing varies by cluster size and support SLAs.
- Private (VPC / on-prem) — licensing + deployment + support:
  - Commercial model: one-time platform fee + annual support & maintenance + optional managed services. Typical enterprise engagements range from $150k to $1M+ ARR depending on scope.

Rules of thumb for sellers:
- Always qualify expected tokens/day and latency requirements before quoting. Example: 100k daily queries at 300 tokens average = ~30M tokens/month — use this to map to hosted vs. dedicated economics.
- Use Dedicated when predictable throughput and data isolation are required (savings and SLA benefit at >25–50M tokens/month depending on model mix).
- Route pricing or discount requests to PricingOps; do not commit to dedicated discounts without legal/pricing approval.

Case studies (two short vignettes for talk tracks)

1) Acme Support (SaaS customer helpdesk) — pilot -> dedicated rollout
- Challenge: Burst traffic during business hours created 95th p50 latency spikes, and per-ticket LLM cost was high.
- Solution: Redwood Dedicated with auto-batching and KV prefix cache; canary rollout and fallback to smaller model during peak events.
- Outcome: 2.3x reduction in per-ticket token costs, 40% reduction in 95th percentile latency, and predictable capacity during seasonal spikes.

2) FinBank (regulated financial services) — Private deployment in VPC + KMS
- Challenge: Strict data residency and encryption requirements prevented hosted models; bank needed consistent inference across branch regions.
- Solution: Private deployment with customer KMS integration, restricted networking, and audit log forwarding to the bank's SIEM.
- Outcome: Compliance requirements satisfied; deployment completed in 10 weeks, with integrated observability allowing operations team to maintain 99.95% uptime SLA for inference endpoints.

Security FAQ (for prospects)

Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: Hosted data is stored in our cloud regions you select (NA/EU/APAC). For regulated customers, we support Private deployments (VPC and on-prem) so data remains in your network. See related page: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention.

Q: How is data protected in transit and at rest?
A: TLS 1.2+ for all in-transit traffic. At rest we use AES-256 encryption; for Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

Q: Do you provide audit logs and access controls?
A: Yes — per-request audit logs, token-level cost attribution, and RBAC via SSO (SAML/OIDC) with SCIM provisioning. Audit logs can be shipped to customer SIEMs.

Q: Certifications and compliance?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and performs annual penetration tests. For enterprise customers we provide compliance paperwork and can support vendor assessments.

Q: Can I run Redwood in an air-gapped environment?
A: Yes — we offer an on-prem package for air-gapped or highly regulated environments under the Private deployment model; standard professional services engagement applies.

Q: What controls exist for model and output governance?
A: Per-route model pinning, canary rollouts, automated fallback policies, and output filters. We also integrate with customer-provided safety tooling during Private deployments.

Sales playbook: discovery and objection handling

- Key discovery questions:
  1) What is your monthly token volume (or expected queries/day and average token length)?
  2) What latency (p50/p95) targets do you need for your user experience?
  3) Do you have data residency, encryption, or audit requirements?
  4) Are you evaluating hosted-only solutions or do you need dedicated/private deployments?
  5) What is your current per-request cost and what saving would justify a migration?

- Common objections + recommended responses:
  - "We can just use cloud managed endpoints": Acknowledge speed of onboarding; emphasize Redwood’s production economics, unified API across private/hosted, and enterprise controls — provide a concrete cost/latency comparison for their workload.
  - "Dedicated/on-prem is complex and slow": Offer a phased pilot (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and highlight our deployment templates and professional services SLA.
  - "Pricing is opaque": Use our transparent guidance and offer a usage worksheet to map tokens to hosted vs dedicated scenarios. Route negotiation to PricingOps.

Technical pilot checklist (SE playbook — numbered steps)

1) Scope & goals: Agree on workload, success metrics (latency targets, cost per request, uptime), and timeline.
2) Data & security: Confirm data residency, sample payloads (sanitized), and network access requirements.
3) Environment: Provision test API keys or a dedicated staging cluster; decide on hosted vs dedicated evaluation.
4) Integration: Implement SDK call patterns, streaming or non-streaming endpoints, and KV caching where appropriate.
5) Observability: Enable per-route tracing, token-level logs, and retention settings.
6) Evaluation: Run load tests (use our benchmarking guide) and capture p50/p95 latency and token costs.
7) Decision: Document go/no-go criteria and recommended next steps (pilot extension, dedicated quoting, or private engagement).
